pairs.evidence: src/components/cli/useTaskQueue.ts:886 A user abort kills the server-side Claude process and then ends the run as a plain failure with no outcomeUnknown flag, even though the server keeps a distinct 'aborted' status; the client also recovers the lost-run case by comparing the error string 'Execution not found' (line 596), so the indeterminate verdict lives in prose instead of a first-class status.

techniques.evidence: src/components/cli/useTaskQueue.ts:596 This is the tell the technique names: the unknown outcome is recovered by matching an error message. endLostRun (line 458) does pass outcomeUnknown, but abort (886) and conflict recovery (741, registerTaskComplete(..., false)) both write failure.

src/components/cli/TerminalInput.tsx:47 The loop here is a one-shot CLI process with no injection point, so mid-unit typed input is refused visibly at the surface ('Working — press Esc to stop…'), which is what the technique's 'when not to reach for this' asks for. Caveat: a programmatic pof-cli-prompt dispatch that arrives while streaming is dropped silently (CompactTerminal.tsx:110).

pairs.evidence: src/app/api/claude-terminal/stream/route.ts:134 When a finished execution is replayed, every non-completed status, including the server's own 'aborted', goes out as an SSE error frame (with no error field), so the client closes an aborted run as a failure; separately, the unknown-outcome case is sent as the error string 'Execution not found' (stream line 106, query line 130), which consumers must string-match.

techniques.evidence: src/app/api/claude-terminal/query/route.ts:130 The lost-execution case, whose outcome is unknown, reaches clients only as an error message string and not as a first-class status. The stream route does the same at line 106.

src/app/api/claude-terminal/query/route.ts:64 Each prompt spawns a fresh CLI execution. The route has no running loop that takes injected input, so the call-boundary injection precondition does not hold.

pairs.evidence: src/app/api/cli-task-registry/route.ts:74 When a new start arrives, a running task whose heartbeat went stale is force-closed as 'failed'. That is a definite verdict about a run nobody observed ending, and the registry vocabulary (running|completed|failed) has no unknown status to write instead.

techniques.evidence: src/app/api/cli-task-registry/route.ts:88 Completion is binary: anything not reported as failed is stored as completed, and a stale run is stored as failed (line 74). No status means 'outcome unknown, not retried'.
